Application Materials.content:
**Documents and information you’ll need**
- a copy of your degree certificate and transcript, or a partial transcript if you’re still studying
- contact details for two academic references
- a personal statement
- an up-to-date CV
- your approved English Language test* (if applicable)
- a letter of sponsorship, if you need one.
* Applicants who have not yet completed an [approved English language test](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/english-language-requirements-2) may apply for a Masters course prior to taking a test.

Interview Requirements.content: Interviews do not form part of the Business School’s standard admissions process. However, in some cases, an applicant may be invited for an interview if it will help inform whether an offer should be made.

Academic Requirements.content:
A Bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons)** or equivalent, usually in **business, management or the social sciences**. **Quantitative skills are desirable but not essential. A willingness to engage with quantitative materials is required.** Those with a degree in a non-business/social science subject will be considered on an individual basis.
**International qualifications:** We accept a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-equivalents-2).
For postgraduate applicants from China: accepted qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school. If the programme asks for **2.1**, applicants from China need **70%-85%, depending on your institution**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
IELTS **6.5 overall, with no less than 6.0 in any component**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course, designed with a progression route to the degree programme. Options include [Language for Business (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k022/language-for-business-6-weeks- "Language for Marketing 6 weeks"), [Language for Business (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k023/language-for-business-10-weeks- "Language for Business: Marketing (10 weeks)"), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).
Application documents include “your approved English Language test* (if applicable).” Applicants who have not yet completed an [approved English language test](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/english-language-requirements-2) may apply for a Masters course prior to taking a test.

Program Overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time). Accredited: Yes.
Developed alongside world-leading experts in data analytics and HR professionals, this innovative course provides you with an in-depth, critical understanding of strategic human resource management, alongside principles and concepts underpinning data science and statistics. In addition to mastering cutting-edge data analytics methods, you’ll gain a practical understanding of how these principles and concepts can be applied in the fields of HR and people management. The course will develop your skills in ‘data translation’. You'll learn how to identify people-related business problems, understand how analytics can provide solutions for these problems and identify and explain actionable insights. You’ll learn alongside inspirational academics, highly qualified teaching staff with extensive research expertise and consultancy experience in the field of HR analytics. You’ll gain knowledge and understanding of advanced HRM concepts.
**Course Highlights**
- This course is shaped by the latest knowledge and critical thinking. Your learning will be informed by cutting edge research into the use of data and analytics in HR, developed at the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) (LIDA), as well as specialist research from the [Centre for Employment Relations, Innovation and Change](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-ceric) (CERIC).
- Gain valuable, real-world insight from high profile industrial guest speakers. Recent speakers have included the former Head of HR for NHS England.
- Graduate with the skills to tackle complex HR and organisational problems through a combination of knowledge of the theory and practice of strategic HRM, and applied statistics and data analysis skills.
- On all Masters courses at Leeds University Business School you’ll have an opportunity to apply for a place on a week-long [international study tour](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fbusiness.leeds.ac.uk%2Fmasters%2Fdoc%2Finternational-study-tour-2&data=05%7C02%7CJ.H.Neary%40leeds.ac.uk%7Ca556d137a1aa4b17380108dca5ad3ca4%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638567410667728266%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=A2qg6C57v7IxUXudS6PCv35kZTyb%2Bl0KrxQSlvJtaRU%3D&reserved=0) which will include company visits, guest lectures and networking events, as well as an opportunity to visit local places of interest. Previous study tours have included visits to Berlin, Frankfurt, Milan and Zurich.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme. As well as giving you the opportunity to build key industry connections, you’ll also develop invaluable professional and practical skills that are highly valued by employers.
Our MSc Data Analytics and HRM is fully accredited by the [Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development](https://www.cipd.org/uk) (CIPD), the only HR institution in the world to recognise HR professionals through chartered membership. This course will allow you to satisfy the entry requirements for associate CIPD membership and chartered CIPD membership (if you have relevant work experience).
There are three core pillars to the taught part of the course: the theory and practice of strategic HRM, the principles of statistics and data analytics and the application of data analytics to HR problems. You'll study these three core areas, as well as being able to choose from several optional modules to suit your interests. In strategic HRM, you'll consider how organisational strategy and context shape ‘good HR’ in functional areas such as workforce planning, recruitment and selection, training and development, and pay and performance management. In data analytics for human resources, you'll study how these principles can be applied in HR. The teaching approach is practical, focusing on helping you to understand how to apply data science and statistics to solve problems in an organisational context.
During your time at Leeds, you'll also attend professional skill workshops as part of your regular timetable. These practical sessions are taught by business professionals and allow you to gain skills and insight to help you cope effectively with the challenges of the world of work upon graduation. You can choose to enhance your studies by opting to gain [Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cipd.co.uk%2F%23gref&data=05%7C01%7CK.Barclay%40leeds.ac.uk%7C60c324f402214dd2a78208daa1f5cb8a%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C1%7C0%7C638000374287231493%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=gBmsNuQj5Oiwf7vswsjz%2FACXiR7p8eovyGf3KqW5WAo%3D&reserved=0) (CIPD) membership alongside your degree.
You’ll be taught using a range of methods including lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops. The rest of your time will be spent in independent learning, allowing you to develop your skills in research and analysis. On this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus. Assessment methods emphasise both knowledge and essential skills development. This may include formal exams, group projects, reports, computer simulation exercises, essays and written assignments, group and individual presentations and reflective logs.
This course will provide you with the academic knowledge and professional skills needed for a career in global human resource management. It will also provide you with the opportunity to specialise in the rapidly developing area of HR analytics. You’ll develop strong analytical and problem-solving skills and become a reflective HR professional. If you're considering further study, the course also provides a solid foundation for a [research degree](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-degrees).
As part of this course, dedicated academic and professional development tutors will provide tailored academic and careers support to help you achieve your career ambitions. You can expect expert advice and guidance on your career choices, help in identifying and applying for jobs and support to boost your employability. You’ll also receive coaching to develop the professional skills you'll need to start a successful career and how to evidence these to prospective employers.
As a Masters student at Leeds, you’ll have the unique opportunity to gain real-world industry experience with the Global Industry Programme. You’ll develop key professional skills and gain invaluable insight into working in your chosen field, helping to solve a real business problem from a live company brief. Benefits include fully online delivery designed to fit around your studies, opportunities to make professional networks, consultancy experience with a UK or international organisation, teamwork across disciplines, putting course teachings into practice, and improving your employability prospects.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The University of Leeds provides estimated living costs as a guideline only, based on average spending. The following estimates are for a single student in 2025, based on the latest data available, and they don’t include tuition fees.
| Cost type | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| University accommodation, self-catered | £117 to £265 |
| University accommodation, catered | £205 to £273 |
| Private accommodation, self-catered | £110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications) |
| Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products | £31 to £38 |
| Household bills: gas and/or electricity, water and broadband internet | £14 to £17 |
| Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone | £44 to £68 |
**Estimated total budget per week: approximately £199 to £423**

Financial Aid.content: International Excellence Scholarships: **£3,000, £6,000 and £16,000 fee reduction scholarships** are available. These scholarships recognise and reward high academic achievement for students who have applied to study a taught Masters course starting in **2026**. Visit the [international Masters scholarships webpage](http://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-scholarships-funding/doc/masters-scholarships) to see what is available, check eligibility and find out how to apply.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Please note that we do not permit deferrals.
